text: Ah, the wick. That slender, braided cord of cotton that serves as the architectural backbone of our domestic despair. It is the primary material of a candle, yes, but let us not be fooled by its humble appearance. This tiny strand is actually the silent witness to our collective failure to engage in long-term planning. While we spend our evenings paralyzed by the existential dread of choosing between Netflix and sleep, the wick stands ready to burn. It is the only thing in the house that consistently delivers on its promises, slowly consuming itself in a tragic, flickering display of commitment. It reminds us that while we are busy complaining about back pain and paying bills, the wick is out here, literally burning the midnight oil, proving that at least one entity in this household has the discipline to stick to a schedule, even if that schedule is just "until I melt into a puddle of wax and regret."
